question: Which exact firmware functions set the scroll direction, snap and scrollbar attributes of an LVGL object and scroll it (relative, absolute x, absolute y)?
callsite_evidence: The firmware's Lua `lvgl` object binding (method table next to the Lua obj methods) names scrollbar_mode, scroll_dir, scroll_snap_x, scroll_snap_y and scroll_by; each name leads to a short setter that writes one bit-field of lv_obj_spec_attr_t (scrollbar_mode bits 0-1, scroll_snap_x bits 2-3, scroll_snap_y bits 4-5, scroll_dir bits 6-9) after the spec_attr allocation helper.

scroll_by is the large function that creates the scroll-x and scroll-y lv_anim records (200..400 ms by viewport size), sends event 9 (SCROLL_BEGIN) and, without animation, forwards to the bounded variant. scroll_to_x / scroll_to_y are the two 0x24-byte wrappers that delete the running animation, read the current scroll (-spec_attr->scroll.x / y) and call the bounded scroll with the difference.
Scroll offsets are read from spec_attr (+32 x, +36 y, negated) by the same getters the lv_obj_scroll_* functions use.
ownership_analysis: The widget is page-owned and the calls run on the UI owner thread, like the other UI host entries.
unsafe_assumptions: The anim argument is lv_anim_enable_t (0 off, 1 on).
recommended_probe: Scroll a module-created container on Mirage and compare with the stock launcher.

artifacts.role: LVGL scroll attribute and scroll functions
